az_alcatraz_wall.blurb: Alcatraz Wall is one of the walls in the Prison Camp area on the lower Catalina Highway side of Mount Lemmon, near Tucson. Six short routes mix a pair of sport lines with four gear climbs, all in an easy-to-moderate range from the mid 5.5s up to 5.8, which makes it a friendly place for newer leaders to practise placing gear or clipping bolts. It faces south and catches lots of sun, so it suits cooler days better than summer. Routes get shorter as the hillside rises to the right. The walk in follows the often-dry creek bed past the neighbouring walls.

az_vineyard_cove.blurb: Vineyard Cove is a small, tucked-away granite alcove on the east side of Cochise Stronghold in southeast Arizona. It holds six routes, a mix of sport, top-rope and one gear line, mostly moderate with a couple of harder lines near 5.10 and one very easy climb. The alcove is shaded in the early morning and again from mid-afternoon, which keeps it bearable in hot months. The walls share chain anchors, so top-roping several lines from one setup is common. From the end of the road the walk in is a level trail of about a minute.

az_pharmacy_the.blurb: The Pharmacy sits at the top of the slot canyon in the Cave Springs section of Oak Creek Canyon in northern Arizona, above The Doctor's Office. It has six routes, mostly sport with a single gear climb, and the grades sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with most of them around 5.11. Climbing is typically on stepped side-pulls and edges, with some sandy, honeycombed patches on the left side. The way up is a short iron-rung via ferrata, with a fixed rope for anyone uneasy on the exposure. It is a good stop for confident sport climbers.

az_west_face_southwest_arete.blurb: The west side of Baboquivari Peak offers a free-climbing alternative to the aid-oriented lines on the east. Six long routes run up the west face and southwest arete, almost all trad with one that also counts as sport, ranging from the easy 5.5 standard route to several nine-pitch 5.10 lines. Expect a committed day: a long drive on a dirt road, then a pack trail through brush to the ledge below the climbs. The rock gets very hot, so pick a cool day. Long pants help on the brushy trail.
